profile.name: Guilherme José
profile.subheadline: I am a Computer Science student dedicated to understanding what happens under the hood—specializing in low-level systems, distributed architectures, operating systems, and scalable infrastructure.

about.sectionSubtitle: Deeply curious about computing abstractions, performance engineering, and system reliability.
paragraphs: I am pursuing a degree in Computer Science with a dedicated specialization in Computer Systems and Infrastructure. My academic and practical focus revolves around how software interfaces directly with hardware, how operating systems manage resources, and how modern distributed systems achieve resilience at scale.

Whether it is writing high-performance code in C, analyzing Linux kernel internals, configuring containerized environments, or reasoning about network protocol overhead, I thrive on demystifying complex abstractions and engineering robust infrastructure foundations.

focusAreas.title: Systems & OS Internals
focusAreas.description: Process scheduling, virtual memory, POSIX interfaces, concurrency primitives, and hardware-software interaction.

focusAreas.title: Distributed Systems & Networks
focusAreas.description: Socket programming, TCP/IP stack, consensus, RPC protocols, and designing fault-tolerant communication pipelines.

focusAreas.title: Infrastructure & DevOps
focusAreas.description: Containerization with Docker, Linux system administration, CI/CD pipelines, and automated environment provisioning.

focusAreas.title: Performance & Diagnostics
focusAreas.description: Benchmarking, memory profiling, profiling system bottlenecks, cache utilization, and observability.
